newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end easier in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end easier in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished lower on Tuesday in thin trade with the market still stuck in a cautious mood, dealers said.
"It's a very thin market and people are not rushing in becase they remain a bit cautious. There were some nibbles from China, but not much was done," a local rubber trader said.
Another dealer said there were several bids and offers during the course of trading, but only a small amount was done in late trade.
"The tonnages done were fairly small. Most of the interest was focused on the forward months," the trader said.

"Some players have shifted their attention to Japan because prices there are cheap," one dealer added. Tokyo's benchmark March contract rose one yen to 134.9 while Kobe's March contract dipped 0.5 yen to 134.4.
At around 0945 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 123.00 U.S. cents a kg from 123.50 cents.

November RSS1 was seen at 175.00-177.00 Singapore cents (US$1.24-$1.26) a kg from yesterday's settlement of 176.75 cents. November TSR20 was seen at 171.00-172.00 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.22) a kg against the previous 172.50 cents.
